leading_positions.synthesis: Seven members (Danielsson, Johansson, Kroll, Lindroth, Mehlig, Olsson, Pearce) name B035 as the basis of their preferred configuration. Eriksson prefers B008 but lists B035 as his first alternative; he is not counted as a supporter here (see the next position). Shared across the B035 supporters: the same two laureates (Katori and Ye), the same reading of the achievement as an idea-plus-realization pair (Katori's magic-wavelength proposal, Ye's push to the 10^-18 regime), independent reproduction at several laboratories, and a view that the attribution is the cleanest on the shortlist. Not shared: whether lattice clocks are distinct enough from the 2005 comb and 2012 ion-control prizes (every supporter lists this as the main reservation), whether the pending redefinition of the second is a necessary or merely supporting argument, how heavily the opening-ballot breadth of support should count, and whether B035 should stand alone (six supporters) or be paired with a second part (Pearce, see below). Citation wording differs slightly: some tie it narrowly to the invention and realization of lattice clocks, others add the 10^-18 regime or timekeeping and precision measurement.

Only Eriksson prefers B008 (Kane, Mele, Molenkamp) as his configuration, on the grounds that it combines a new organizing principle (Z2 topology), a rapid decisive experiment in HgTe and field-wide consequences. He also states he would not defend B008 against a well-argued shift to B035 because of the credit problem. Other members rate B008 as a strong alternative (Danielsson, Johansson, Lindroth, Mehlig, Olsson and Pearce list it as an alternative) and Mehlig argues it is arguably the more far-reaching science, but none of them prefers it in their configuration. What is not shared: the weight given to the missing proposers of the HgTe route (Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang), the deceased status of Zhang, the three-dimensional generalisation outside the credit set, and overlap with the 2016 prize.

Only Pearce proposes a two-part configuration: B035 (Katori and Ye) together with B023 (Halzen alone, for conception and leadership of IceCube and the discovery of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos). The B035 part is shared with the other seven members; the B023 part is not endorsed by anyone else. Pearce himself flags the one-name credit as an attribution compromise, since Karle and Spiering are named on the B023 ballot, and notes that his own field proximity and Fermi-LAT follow-up connections should be weighed. Danielsson, in a response to Pearce, ranks IceCube below the other candidates because the origin of most of the flux is unresolved and water-based confirmation is incomplete.

areas_of_agreement: Eight of eight members proposed Katori and Ye as the laureate pair for B035 at the opening stage, and in round 1 seven prefer B035 explicitly while Eriksson lists it as his first alternative.

Seven of eight members prefer B035 as their round-1 configuration, and at least Danielsson, Johansson and Mehlig moved to it from a different opening first choice or a lower rank after reading the other ballots.

Members agree on the shape of the scientific case for B035: Katori's magic-wavelength idea removes the light-shift problem, Ye's group brought the clocks to the 10^-18 level, and several independent laboratories (JILA, RIKEN and Tokyo, PTB, SYRTE, NIST) reproduce the performance.
All members who discuss B035 accept that the redefinition of the second is under discussion and not yet decided.
Members agree that the main reservation is overlap with earlier recognised work: the 2005 prize for frequency combs and the 2012 prize for control of single trapped ions.
Members who discuss B008 (Danielsson, Eriksson, Mehlig, Olsson) agree that the HgTe credit (Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang) is the central difficulty for that proposal.
scientific_disputes: Whether lattice clocks are a distinct invention (Danielsson and Kroll argue the physical concept of interrogating a large ensemble in a magic-wavelength lattice differs from a single-ion clock) or an excellent refinement of a toolkit already recognised in 2005 and 2012 (a reservation every B035 supporter and Eriksson record).

Whether B035 as precision measurement outweighs a conceptual shift: Mehlig and Danielsson hold that B008 (new class of matter) or B006 (Higgs discovery) is arguably higher in pure scientific significance, while the B035 supporters stress breadth of consequence in tests of fundamental constants, relativistic geodesy and dark-matter searches.

Whether the diffuse high-energy neutrino flux in B023 is a sufficient discovery claim, given that source identification (TXS 0506+056, NGC 1068) is at modest significance and water-based confirmation from KM3NeT and Baikal-GVD is incomplete (raised by Pearce and Danielsson).
Whether the 2016 prize for topological phases of matter overlaps with the Z2 topological insulator work in B008 (Danielsson sees more overlap than Mehlig; Eriksson sees it as distinct).
attribution_disputes: For B035, the two names are agreed, but Danielsson, Johansson, Kroll, Lindroth, Mehlig, Olsson and Pearce all note that Lemonde, Takamoto and the Sr and Yb groups at SYRTE, PTB and NIST (and, for some, ion-clock groups) contributed materially and are outside a two-name prize. Members differ on whether this is fatal (none say so) or whether citation wording alone, tied to invention and realization, is enough (Danielsson, Lindroth).

For B035, Kroll and Mehlig ask whether Ye's credit is for the lattice-clock realization specifically or for a wider programme in combs, ultracold matter and many-body spectroscopy, and whether the citation should centre on the magic-wavelength concept or on the 10^-18 performance. Lindroth also notes Ye's role is partly a continuation of a programme already recognised in 2005.

For B008, Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang proposed the HgTe route that Molenkamp measured and are not credited; Zhang is deceased; and the 3D generalisation (Fu, Kane, Mele; Moore and Balents; Hasan) is outside the three names (Danielsson, Eriksson, Mehlig, Olsson).
For B004, Girvin and Huang are noted as missing from the credit (raised in Danielsson's response to Johansson); Johansson prefers B004 only as an alternative in round 1.

For B023, only one of Halzen, Karle and Spiering fits beside Katori and Ye in a three-name limit; Pearce flags that Halzen alone omits Karle and Spiering, and Danielsson calls a collaboration-scale prize with three names an arbitrary selection.
maturity_disputes: Whether the redefinition of the second must be decided before a lattice-clock prize (Johansson, Kroll and Olsson say the case would be stronger or that the committee might wait; Danielsson, Lindroth, Mehlig and Pearce treat it as supporting rather than necessary).
Whether the 2025 prize for superconducting circuits should discount circuit QED (B004) and whether that discount fades within a few years (Johansson).
Whether IceCube (B023) is mature enough while the origin of most of the flux is unresolved and independent water-based confirmation is incomplete (Pearce and Danielsson).

Whether the opening-ballot breadth of support for B035 (six top-three placements, two first places, all eight ranking it) is information about merit or only about how the opening ballots happened to fall (Johansson and Mehlig treat it as a signal to be tested and not as merit in itself; Kroll and Lindroth cite it as evidence of support across subfields).
conflict_or_recusal_flags: Johansson: circuit QED (B004) is his own research field; he directs WACQT, which builds on the cQED architecture; Chalmers colleagues Delsing and Wilson work in the area. No personal tie to Blais, Wallraff or Schoelkopf is recorded. He suggests his views on B004 be weighed with this interest in mind.

Olsson: she is at Chalmers, as is Johansson, whose field is the subject of B004, and says she would consider recusing herself from that part of any deliberation; her field of electron microscopy may also bias her toward B019, which she ranked first in the opening but does not propose here.

Kroll: he spent time in John Hall's laboratory in Boulder, part of the frequency-comb background of the JILA environment where Ye works; he knows of no tie to Katori or Ye personally; his WACQT and quantum-memory background touches B004 and B015.

Lindroth: she collaborates with Anne L'Huillier's Lund attosecond group and with Ursula Keller's group at ETH Zurich, the institution of Wallraff (B004); she describes this as not a direct tie to B004 but would disclose it if circuit QED became a leading option.

Pearce (Chair): documented connections to the Fermi-LAT and PAMELA collaborations and astroparticle work at KTH; he is not recorded as belonging to IceCube but flags B023 as a potential proximity issue because of Fermi-LAT follow-up of TXS 0506+056. His own configuration is the only one that includes B023.
Eriksson: his electronic-structure and magnetism work is adjacent to B008 and B051, which he says may bias him, but he records no personal or institutional tie to a credited candidate.
Danielsson and Mehlig record no specific conflict.
questions_for_round2: Does the committee treat optical lattice clocks (B035) as a distinct invention from the 2005 comb and 2012 ion-control prizes, and what specific physical step (magic-wavelength lattice, Lamb-Dicke interrogation of many atoms, control of many-body effects) makes it so?

Should the B035 citation rest on the magic-wavelength concept, on the 10^-18 performance, or both, and does the answer settle the credit between Katori (concept and first Sr clocks) and Ye (performance and systematics) without leaving out Lemonde, Takamoto and the other Sr and Yb groups?

Is B035 sufficient as a single two-name prize, or should a second part (B023 as Pearce proposes, or B008 as Eriksson prefers) be added? If so, which of the three possible third names or one-name credits can be defended?

For B023 alone, should the credit go to Halzen alone, to Halzen and Karle, or to all three of Halzen, Karle and Spiering, and is the discovery claim restricted to the diffuse flux given that source identification is at modest significance?
For B008, can a citation within three names handle the Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang proposal and the 3D topological-insulator work, and does the 2016 prize leave room for the Z2 insulator?
How much weight should the pending redefinition of the second carry for B035: must the committee wait for the metrology decision, or is the existing reproduction across laboratories enough?
Given the disclosures from Johansson, Olsson, Kroll, Lindroth and Pearce, does the committee wish to record any recusal or limit on participation for B004, B023 or B035 before the final ballot?
summary.chair_observation: Seven of eight members explicitly prefer B035 in round 1, and all eight propose the same two laureates. The remaining open points are not whether B035 is a strong candidate but whether it overlaps too closely with the 2005 and 2012 prizes, how the many contributing clock groups should be reflected in the citation, and whether a second part (B023 or B008) should be added. Eriksson prefers B008 and Pearce adds B023; neither is a majority position, and the committee should not read agreement on B035 as agreement on any second part.
